title: Tail Cues, Principal Corrections: Plug-and-Play Rectification for Open-Set Test-Time Adaptation
claim: Our lightweight plug-in alone beats existing methods on accuracy, runtime and memory, and cheaply lifts every method it attaches to.
layout: 1 wide bubble scatter, runtime x vs score y, arrows from baseline to +plug-in
description: A single wide bubble chart with runtime in minutes on the x-axis (nonlinear ticks) and H-score on the y-axis. Each baseline (Source, COME, UniEnt, OSTTA, SAR, STAMP, CoTTA, ViDA) is a circle in its own color. Circle area encodes GPU memory, and the MiB value is written in the label. Colored arrows run from each baseline to its +TALOR variant. These variants sit higher and are usually only slightly larger. A bold dashed green horizontal line marks Source+TALOR, the standalone plug-in. The tiny green Source+TALOR point sits at far left, above most baselines. The background fades from green at the top to peach at the bottom, so the upper left reads as best. The eye goes first to the dashed line and the small green points at upper left.
caption: Runtime--performance--memory comparison of TALOR and representative baselines. Circle size denotes GPU usage. The dashed line marks Source+TALOR: even as a standalone plug-in, it surpasses existing methods while using the least runtime and memory. When attached to other TTA methods, TALOR substantially improves their performance with only marginal additional budgets.
abstract: Open-Set Test-Time Adaptation (OSTTA) operates on non-stationary target streams where covariate and semantic shifts coexist. Existing TTA methods often obtain adaptation signals by updating model parameters or maintaining mutable memories, which can be costly and vulnerable to unknown samples. We present TALOR, a lightweight, backward-free rectification module that uses the source linear head as a geometric anchor. The head-induced basis decomposes each normalized feature into high-gain principal coordinates and low-gain tail coordinates. TALOR estimates a soft-routed affine correction in the principal subspace, combining a regime-level principal bias with a tail-conditioned slope that captures sample-level tail-to-principal coupling. Using weighted ridge regression, it subtracts this drift estimate from the principal coordinates, reconstructs the feature and feeds it into the source head. On the ImageNet-C benchmark with six csOOD datasets, TALOR outperforms the next-best UniEnt by 2.2% H-score while running 2.5x faster and using only 12% of its GPU memory; as a post-correction plug-in, it further boosts COME to 68.4% H-score with only 2% additional memory overhead.
